What is the atomic number of Unbihexium?
Unbihexium, also known as element 126 or eka-plutonium, is a hypothetical chemical element; it has atomic number 126 and placeholder symbol Ubh.
In what year was Steve Jobs born?
Steve Jobs: Steven Paul Jobs (February 24, 1955 – October 5, 2011) was an American businessman, inventor, and investor.
In what year was Silver discovered?
Silver is a chemical element; it has symbol Ag (from Latin argentum 'silver') and atomic number 47.
In what year was Manganese discovered?
Manganese is a chemical element; it has the symbol Mn and atomic number 25.
Which company manufactures LTV A-7 Corsair II?
LTV A-7 Corsair II: Ling-Temco-Vought. The LTV A-7 Corsair II is an American carrier-capable subsonic light attack aircraft designed and manufactured by Ling-Temco-Vought (LTV).
In which country is Junkers Ju 52?
Junkers Ju 52: Germany. Development of the Ju 52 commenced in the late 1920s, headed by German aeronautical engineer Ernst Zindel.
Who is credited with discovering Plutonium?
Plutonium: Glenn Theodore Seaborg. Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
Who is credited with discovering Fermium?
Fermium: Glenn Theodore Seaborg. Fermium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fm and atomic number 100.
Who is credited with discovering Sodium?
Sodium: Humphry Davy. Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na (from Neo-Latin natrium) and atomic number 11.
This long-term skin condition occurs when dead skin cells and oil clog hair follicles, producing blackheads, whiteheads, and pimples mainly on the face, chest, and back — what is it?
Acne is a long-term skin condition that occurs when dead skin cells and sebum clog hair follicles.
This large, muscular mastiff-type dog breed descends from ancestors brought to the British North American colonies, where they worked on small farms and ranches — what's the breed?
American Bulldog is a large, muscular breed of mastiff-type dog.
With 1,248 built, this turboprop's design was adapted from an earlier Soviet transport aircraft and became NATO's 'Cub' — which four-engine workhorse?
Antonov An-12 (NATO reporting name: Cub) is a four-engined turboprop transport aircraft designed in the Soviet Union.
Once native to the highland lakes of Xochimilco and Chalco, this neotenic mole salamander keeps its external gills and stays aquatic for life — what is it?
Axolotl (from Classical; Ambystoma mexicanum) is a species of mole salamander.

The bassist of a legendary British rock band from 1962 to 1993, performing on its first 19 studio albums, this musician was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1989 as part of that group — who is he?
Bill Wyman (n Perks; born 24 October 1936) is an English musician who was the bassist of the rock band the Rolling Stones from 1962 to 1993.
This rhythmic bodily process draws oxygen-rich air into the lungs and expels carbon dioxide, powering the cellular chemistry that turns food into energy — what process is it?
Breathing (respiring or ventilating) is the rhythmic process of inhaling air into the lungs providing oxygen, and exhaling the air removing carbon dioxide, in the gas exchange process.
Prized in India for hashish and cultivated from China to West Africa, this Hindu Kush-native plant produces cannabinoid levels well above ordinary hemp — which species?
Cannabis indica is an annual plant species in the family Cannabaceae indigenous to the Hindu Kush mountains of Southern Asia.
Built under license from the Soviet MiG-21, this Chinese fighter jet carries the NATO reporting name Fishcan and specializes in short-range air combat — what aircraft is it?
Chengdu J-7 (pinyin: Jin-7; third generation export version J-7; NATO reporting name: Fishcan) is a Chinese fighter aircraft.
The smallest member of the cockatoo family, this Australian parrot is recognized for its expressive crest and long tail feathers, and is a hugely popular pet bird. What bird is it?

Cockatiel (Nymphicus hollandicus), also known as the weero/weiro or quarrion, is a species of small- to medium-sized parrot belonging to the cockatoo family (Cacatuidae), of which it is the smallest member.

This family of fifteen tall, long-necked bird species mostly wears muted gray-and-white plumage with a patch of bare red skin on the face — except for one crowned genus that stands out — what bird is it?
Crane (bird) are a type of large bird with long legs and necks in the biological family Gruidae of the order Gruiformes.
This colourless, highly volatile, sweet-smelling organic compound with formula (CH3CH2)2O was once used as a general anesthetic and remains a common laboratory solvent — what is it?
This American physicist was the first to make a transuranium element, neptunium, sharing the 1951 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Glenn Seaborg. Who was he?
Edwin McMillan (September 18, 1907 - September 7, 1991) was an American physicist credited with being the first to produce a transuranium element, neptunium.

This branch of anthropology systematically studies individual cultures from the point of view of the people within them, relying heavily on researchers directly participating in the settings they study — what is this method called?
Ethnography is a branch of anthropology and the systematic study of individual cultures. It explores cultural phenomena from the point of view of the subject of the study.
The lightest halogen, this pale yellow gas is so reactive it combines with nearly every other element except the light noble gases. What element is it (symbol F)?
Fluorine is a chemical element; it has the symbol F and atomic number 9.
With the symbol Ge and atomic number 32, this lustrous, brittle metalloid was predicted to exist by Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869, decades before it was actually discovered — name this element?
Germanium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ge and atomic number 32.
This North Atlantic member of the true cod family is a fisheries staple in northern Europe, often smoked into varieties like Finnan haddie and the Arbroath smokie — what is it?
Haddock (Melanogrammus aeglefinus) is a saltwater ray-finned fish from the family Gadidae, the true cods.

This extinct human species from the Middle Pleistocene may represent the last common ancestor of modern humans, Neanderthals, and Denisovans — or a completely separate lineage altogether — what species is it?
Homo heidelbergensis is a species of archaic human from the Middle Pleistocene of Europe and Africa, as well as potentially Asia depending on the taxonomic convention used.
This Russian-American aviation pioneer, a trailblazer in both helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft, won the top prize at the 1912 Moscow Aviation Exhibition for one of his early designs — who is he?
Igor Sikorsky (25 May 1889 - 26 October 1972) was a Russian-American aviation pioneer in both helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft.

Designed under the philosophy 'write once, run anywhere,' this high-level, memory-safe, object-oriented programming language compiles to bytecode executed by a dedicated virtual machine — name the language?
Java (programming language) is a high-level, general-purpose, memory-safe, object-oriented programming language.
This pain-relieving, fever-reducing drug belongs to the propionic acid class of anti-inflammatories and hit the market in 1980, thirteen years after being patented — what is it?
Ketoprofen is one of the propionic acid class of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAID) with analgesic and antipyretic effects.
This American computer scientist won the 2013 Turing Award for taming the chaos of distributed systems — and, on the side, created the document-preparation system LaTeX — who is he?
Leslie Lamport (born February 7, 1941) is an American computer scientist and mathematician.
This paired organ, located near the backbone on either side of the heart in most mammals, extracts oxygen from the air and releases carbon dioxide back into it — name the organ?
Lung are the primary organs of the respiratory system in many animals, including humans.
Working on the geometry of Riemann surfaces, this Tehran-born Stanford professor became in 2014 the first woman and first Iranian to win the Fields Medal — who was she?
Maryam Mirzakhani (12 May 1977 - 14 July 2017) was an Iranian mathematician and a professor of mathematics at Stanford University.
Carrying NATO's 'Hind' codename and its crews' affectionate 'flying tank,' this Soviet machine is both an attack craft and a low-capacity troop carrier. What is it?
Mil Mi-24 (NATO reporting name: Hind) is a large helicopter gunship, attack helicopter and low-capacity troop transport with room for eight passengers.

In this group of bone-marrow cancers, blood cells fail to mature properly and never develop into healthy cells, early on there are often no symptoms, though it can progress into acute leukemia. Name the condition?
Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) is one of a group of cancers in which blood cells in the bone marrow do not mature, and as a result, do not develop into healthy blood cells.
This American nuclear-capable subsonic stealth bomber, solely operated by the US Air Force, is designed as a flying wing to penetrate sophisticated air defenses. What is this aircraft?
Northrop B-2 Spirit is an American nuclear-capable subsonic stealth strategic bomber, often referred to as a "stealth bomber", solely operated by the United States Air Force.
It surges during childbirth and sexual activity, drives maternal bonding and milk production, and is released by the posterior pituitary — which hormone is this?
Oxytocin is a peptide hormone and neuropeptide normally produced in the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary.
This inflammation of the lining of the abdominal cavity can be caused by a ruptured appendix, a perforated ulcer, or pancreatitis, and may lead to shock if untreated. What condition is it?
Peritonitis is inflammation of the localized or generalized peritoneum, the lining of the inner wall of the abdomen and covering of the abdominal organs.
Caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis and often spread by flea bites, this disease comes in pneumonic, bubonic, and septicemic forms — what is it?
Plague (disease) is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. There are three forms of plague, each affecting a different part of the body and causing associated symptoms.
Used to treat high blood pressure, irregular heart rhythms, performance anxiety and migraine prevention, this beta blocker medication reaches the bloodstream within 30 minutes of dosing — which drug?
Propranolol is a medication of the beta blocker class. It can be taken orally, rectally, or by intravenous injection.

One of 36 species-rich pit vipers found mainly in the Americas, this snake shakes a noisy tail segment to warn off predators and is responsible for most snakebite injuries in North America — which snake?
Rattlesnake are venomous snakes that form the genera Crotalus and Sistrurus of the subfamily Crotalinae (the pit vipers).

Known by folk names like knotberry and lowbush salmonberry, this amber fruit structurally similar to a blackberry thrives in Arctic tundra and boreal forest but isn't farmed commercially — which species?
Rubus chamaemorus (also known as cloudberry) is a species of flowering plant in the rose family, Rosaceae.
This interdisciplinary field studies signs and sign systems, breaking down into branches examining the formal relations between signs, their meanings, and their users — what's the field called?
Semiotics is the study of signs. It is an interdisciplinary field that examines what signs are, how they form sign systems, and how individuals use them to communicate meaning.
This plant family includes both deadly poisonous species and kitchen staples like tomatoes, potatoes, and peppers, all linked by unusually high alkaloid content — what family is it?
Solanaceae is a family of flowering plants in the order Solanales.
In the equation 5 − 2 = 3, this is the operation being performed — which one is it?
Subtraction (which is signified by the minus sign) is one of the four arithmetic operations along with addition, multiplication and division.

This mass of gray matter forming part of the forebrain relays sensory and motor signals to the cerebral cortex through radiating nerve fibers, and helps regulate consciousness, sleep, and alertness — what's the structure?
Thalamus (pl.: thalami; from Greek, "chamber") is a large mass of gray matter on the lateral wall of the third ventricle forming the dorsal part of the diencephalon (a division of the forebrain).
Taken by mouth, injection, or inhalation, this steroid helps prevent asthma and COPD flare-ups from worsening — which medication?
Triamcinolone is a glucocorticoid used to treat certain skin diseases, allergies, and rheumatic disorders among others.
Its Latin name means 'maiden,' and it's the largest zodiac grouping in the sky, home to the bright star Spica between Leo and Libra — which one?
Virgo (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac. The ecliptic intersects the celestial equator within this constellation and Pisces.

An Iranian-born American surgeon specializing in bariatric and vascular procedures, this reality TV doctor became known for helping morbidly obese patients lose weight on the long-running series My 600-lb Life — name this doctor?

A rapid rise-and-fall of voltage across a cell membrane, this "spike" depolarizes neighboring spots and is how neurons and muscle cells fire — what is this electrical event called?
Action potential: Neuron communication by electric impulses.
Beginning about six hours after someone dependent on drinking stops, this set of symptoms can include shaking, sweating, seizures, and life-threatening delirium -- what is it called?
Over 500 of these organic compounds exist in nature, yet only 22 appear in the genetic code, joining together to build proteins — what are they?
Amino acid: Organic compounds containing amine and carboxylic groups.
Awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2008 for his AIDS-relief work on PEPFAR, this immunologist directed the U.S. allergy and infectious-disease institute from 1984 to 2022. Who is he?
Known as common wormwood, this bitter herb native to North Africa and temperate Eurasia lends its name and flavor to a notorious green spirit — which plant?
Artemisia absinthium: Species of plant. It is grown as an ornamental plant and is used as an ingredient in the spirit absinthe and some other alcoholic beverages.
Whose name derives from the Sanskrit word 'nimba,' this Mahogany-family tree native to South Asia is the source of a widely used pesticidal oil — which species, and not one of these animals?
Azadirachta indica: Species of plant. Azadirachta indica, commonly known as neem, margosa, nimtree or Indian lilac, is a tree in the Mahogany family Meliaceae.
Commonly known as barberry, this genus of deciduous and evergreen shrubs grows worldwide except Australia, and one of its species is Oregon's official state flower — what genus is it?
Berberis: Genus of flowering plants representing the barberry family.
Credited with kicking off the Jet Age, this swept-wing quadjet airliner entered regular passenger service with Pan Am in October 1958 — which aircraft?

He won a share of the 1973 Nobel Prize in Physics for an effect he discovered as a Cambridge PhD student in 1962 — then, in the 1970s, took up Transcendental Meditation and pursued ideas beyond mainstream science. Who is he?
Its dihydrate form is the mineral gypsum and its dehydrated cousin is bassanite; sparingly soluble, it causes permanent hardness in water — which inorganic salt is this?
Calcium sulfate: Chemical derived from gypsum used in food and industry.
A nerve compression syndrome caused when the median nerve in the wrist becomes compressed, causing numbness and tingling in the thumb and fingers. What is this condition?
Carpal tunnel syndrome: Compression of the median nerve in the wrist. It can also be measured with electrodiagnostic tests.
India's third lunar mission carried a lander named Vikram and a rover, both replacing equivalents lost when the previous mission crashed on landing. What was the rover called?

Chandrayaan-3 is the third mission in ISRO's Chandrayaan lunar-exploration programme, consisting of the lander Vikram and the rover Pragyan, replacements for the equivalents on Chandrayaan-2, which crashed on landing.
In this chronic liver condition, healthy tissue is replaced by scar tissue and regenerative nodules, choking blood flow and causing portal hypertension — what is it called?
Cirrhosis: Chronic disease of the liver, characterized by fibrosis.
In mathematics, this is a selection of items from a set where the order of choosing them does not matter, unlike a permutation — what is it called?

Combination: Selection of items from a set. In mathematics, a combination is a selection of items from a set that has distinct members, such that the order of selection does not matter (unlike permutations).
Domesticated in Africa and thriving in sandy, low-rainfall soil, this ancient legume is now grown mostly in Nigeria and Niger, which together supply two-thirds of the world's crop — which plant?
Cowpea: Species of plant. The cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) is an annual herbaceous legume from the genus Vigna.
Son of a bass-baritone and born into a family of engineers, this American built his first car at 19, won four F1 Grands Prix, and took Le Mans in 1967 — who was he?
Dan Gurney: American racing driver, engineer and motorsport executive (1931–2018)
Nicknamed 'dumb cane' because its poisonous sap can temporarily rob you of speech, this shade-tolerant tropical houseplant is native to the New World — which genus?
Dieffenbachia: Genus of plants. Dieffenbachia, commonly known as dumb cane or leopard lily, is a genus of tropical flowering plants in the family Araceae.
This plant genus in the mallow family produces the world's most famously pungent fruit, alongside eight other edible-fruit-bearing species — which genus?
Durio: Genus of plants. Several species produce an edible fruit known as durian, the most common species being Durio zibethinus, with eight others producing edible fruit.

The heaviest aircraft ever built by its Brazilian manufacturer, this twin-engine jet transport was developed as a derivative of a regional jetliner, similar in role to the C-130 Hercules. Which aircraft?
Embraer C-390 Millennium: Brazilian military transport aircraft/tanker.
The simplest alkene and the most-produced organic compound on Earth, this colorless gas is also a natural plant hormone used to ripen fruit — what is it?
This principle describes how a changing magnetic field generates an electric current, underpinning the operation of transformers, generators, and motors — what is it called?
Faraday's law of induction: Basic law of electromagnetism.
The lightest halogen, this pale yellow gas is so reactive that several 19th-century chemists died or were injured trying to isolate it, until Henri Moissan finally succeeded in 1886 — which element?
Fluorine: Chemical element with atomic number 9 (F)
Tucked beneath the liver, this pear-shaped organ stores and concentrates bile before releasing it to aid fat digestion in the small intestine — which organ?
Gallbladder: Organ in humans and other vertebrates.
The tallest land animal alive and the largest ruminant on Earth, its closest living relative is the okapi — which long-necked African mammal is it?
Unlike its rocky, mountain-dwelling marmot relatives, this solitary lowland rodent — also called the woodchuck — is common across the Eastern U.S., Canada, and Alaska. What is it?
Groundhog: Species of rodent. The groundhog (Marmota monax), also known as the woodchuck, is a rodent of the family Sciuridae, belonging to the group of large ground squirrels known as marmots.

Often defined as the normal functioning of the body free of disease, pain, or injury, this multidimensional state of well-being can be promoted by exercise and sleep and harmed by smoking or stress — what's the one-word concept?
Health: Desirable level of functional or metabolic efficiency of a living being.
Named for the English physician who first described it in 1832, this cancer is defined by multinucleated Reed–Sternberg cells in the lymph nodes — what is it?
Hodgkin lymphoma: Type of blood and immune-system cancer.
This immune response causes tissue damage upon repeated exposure to an antigen and underlies conditions like hay fever, which affects roughly one in ten people worldwide — what is it called?
Hypersensitivity: Overreaction of the immune system to an antigen.
This sugar alcohol, with about half the sweetness of table sugar, is made by the human kidney at roughly two grams a day and reaches its highest concentration in the brain — what is it?
Inositol: Carbocyclic sugar. Its formula is C6H12O6; the molecule has a ring of six carbon atoms, each with a hydrogen atom and a hydroxy group (–OH).
This fragrant genus of shrubs and vines in the olive family is grown in vast quantities in one Egyptian village that supplies much of the world's perfume industry — which plant?
Jasmine: Genus of flowering plant in the olive family Oleaceae.
Born Giulia Maddalena Angela in Italy, this physician became a leading freethinker and activist for women's rights and social reform in early-20th-century Argentina — who is she?
Julieta Lanteri: Argentine doctor and activist (1873–1932)
Nocturnal, owl-faced, and unable to fly, this endangered New Zealand bird holds the title of the world's heaviest parrot. What is it?
Kākāpō: Parrot endemic to New Zealand. It is the only parrot to have a polygynous lek breeding system.
This synthetic thyroid hormone treats hypothyroidism, has a half-life of roughly 7.5 days, and is not intended for weight loss — what's this medication?
Levothyroxine: Thyroid hormone medication. Levothyroxine, also known as L-thyroxine, is a synthetic form of the thyroid hormone thyroxine (T4).
Sold as Ativan, this benzodiazepine treats anxiety, insomnia, and active seizures, and is even used during surgery to interfere with memory formation — what medication is it?
Lorazepam: Benzodiazepine medication. Lorazepam, sold under the brand name Ativan among others, is a benzodiazepine medication.
Produced when beta-amylase breaks starch down two glucose units at a time, which reducing disaccharide gets its name from the germinating-seed process of malting?
Grown from the YF-17 that lost the Air Force's lightweight fighter contest, which twin-engine carrier jet won a second life when the Navy picked it instead?
McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet: American carrier-capable multirole strike aircraft.
A physician-turned-hedge-fund-manager, this investor famously predicted the subprime mortgage crisis and was portrayed in the 2015 film The Big Short — who is he?
Michael Burry: American hedge fund manager (born 1971)
Nicknamed 'water warts,' this viral skin infection causes small pink bumps with a telltale dimple in the center and usually clears up on its own within a year — what is it?

Molluscum contagiosum: Viral infection of the skin. Molluscum contagiosum (MC), sometimes called water warts, is a viral infection of the skin that results in small raised pink lesions with a dimple in the center.
This lipid-rich substance wraps around nerve axons in segments, leaving gaps called nodes of Ranvier that let electrical signals leap along in a process called saltatory conduction — what is it?
Myelin: Fatty substance insulating nerve cell axons.

This silvery-white transition metal with a faint golden tinge resists corrosion thanks to a thin oxide layer, and in pure native form it's mostly found inside iron meteorites — which element, atomic number 28, is it?
Nickel: Chemical element with atomic number 28 (Ni)
This soft-bodied mollusc can radically deform its shape to squeeze through tiny gaps and propels itself backward by jetting water through a siphon — what eight-limbed creature is it?
Octopus: Soft-bodied eight-limbed order of molluscs.
Sold under the brand name Anavar, this synthetic anabolic steroid helps burn victims and Turner syndrome patients gain weight — what is it?
Oxandrolone: Androgen and anabolic steroid. It was sold under the brand names Oxandrin and Anavar, among others.
First domesticated in Neolithic China, this tree's fruit comes in a fuzzy form and a glossy-skinned twin called the nectarine — what fruit, a rose-family relative of the cherry and plum?
Peach: Type of fruit tree, or its fruit.
The body produces about a quart of this substance daily to trap airborne particles and bacteria — coughed up, it's also known as sputum. What is it?
Phlegm: Mucus produced by the respiratory system (excluding the nasal passages)
Commonly called frangipani, this fragrant flowering shrub native to Mexico and the Caribbean is now a beloved ornamental in Hawaii and desert climates of Arabia — what genus is it?
Plumeria: Genus of flowering plants endemic to the Americas.
Defined as supervising a team to hit all its goals within three primary constraints — scope, time, and budget — what is this discipline?
Project management: Practice of leading the work of a team to achieve goals and criteria at a specified time.

Found across Africa, Asia, and Australia, this family of nonvenomous snakes — including some of the world's largest — must coil around prey and squeeze it into cardiac arrest before swallowing it whole. What is the family?
Pythonidae: Family of snakes. The taxonomy of pythons has evolved, and they are now known to be more closely related to sunbeam snakes and the Mexican burrowing python.

Nicknamed 'the Thud' by its crews, this Mach 2 jet flew most of the early Vietnam War's strike missions and became the only American aircraft ever pulled from combat over unsustainable losses — which plane?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief: US Air Force supersonic fighter-bomber.
Native to tropical Africa and the Indian subcontinent, this medium-sized parrot has established wild populations worldwide after pet-trade escapees adapted brilliantly to city life — which bird?

Rose-ringed parakeet: Species of bird. The rose-ringed parakeet (Psittacula krameri), also known as the ring-necked parakeet, is a medium-sized parrot in the genus Psittacula, of the family Psittaculidae.
This Sapporo-born programmer rose to become Nintendo's fourth president, betting on novel, entertaining games over the most powerful hardware — who is he?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Satoru Iwata: Japanese video game executive (1959–2015)
Domesticated more than 3,000 years ago and prized for having one of the highest oil contents of any seed, which crop is also known as benne?
Sesame: Plant cultivated for its edible seeds.

Once extracted from the ashes of certain salt-absorbing plants and now produced from ordinary salt and limestone via the Solvay process, this alkaline compound is also known as washing soda or soda ash — what is it?
Sodium carbonate: Chemical compound. Sodium carbonate (also known as washing soda, soda ash, sal soda, and soda crystals) is the inorganic compound with the formula Na2CO3 and its various hydrates.
Also known as asteroids for belonging to the class Asteroidea, this marine invertebrate typically has a central disc and five arms — what is it?
Starfish: Class of echinoderms, marine animal.
Despite the naming confusion with true yams, this starchy tuberous root actually belongs to the morning glory family and hails from tropical Ecuador — which crop?
Sweet potato: Species of edible plant.
Famously nicknamed 'white ants,' these wood-munching eusocial insects are actually genetically closer to cockroaches than they are to true ants — what are they?
Termite: Social insects related to cockroaches.
He joined Apple in 1998 to run worldwide operations and stepped up to the top job in 2011 when Steve Jobs resigned — which executive now leads the company?
Estimated to date back to the end of the Jurassic period roughly 156 million years ago, this fungal genus includes several species of truffles prized as culinary delicacies — which genus?
Tuber (fungus): Genus of fungi. Tuber is a genus in the fungal family Tuberaceae, with estimated molecular dating to the end of the Jurassic period (156 Mya).
The primary flavor compound in the vanilla bean, this phenolic aldehyde is now more often made synthetically than extracted from the real pod — what is it?
Vanillin: Chemical compound. Vanillin is an organic compound with the molecular formula C8H8O3.
Native to the Baltic, Black, and Caspian Sea basins, this large freshwater fish's range now stretches from the UK to western China — which species?
Wels catfish: Species of fish. It has been introduced to several countries in Western Europe, Mediterranean and Asia as a prized sport fish.
Following her husband's death, this Russian economist and activist vowed to carry on his opposition work and now chairs the Human Rights Foundation — who is she?
Yulia Navalnaya: Russian economist and political activist (born 1976)
